title: Impersonal verbs: falloir, pleuvoir, neiger
goal: By the end of this lesson you can use impersonal verbs with il in every tense you know (il faut, il pleut, il neige, il fait froid, il y a) and understand the Quebec weather talk you hear every day: faut que, y mouille, y fait frette.

body: Some verbs are only used with *il*, and this *il* means 'it', not 'he': *il faut* (it is necessary), *il pleut* (it's raining), *il neige* (it's snowing), *il grêle* (it's hailing), *il gèle* (it's freezing).

Other verbs can also be used impersonally: *il fait* + weather (*il fait beau, il fait froid*), *il y a* (there is/are), *il est* + time (*il est huit heures*), *il reste* (there is … left), *il manque* (… is missing).
*Il faut* + infinitive means 'you have to / we need to / one must', with no specific person: *Il faut partir* (We have to go). *Il ne faut pas* means 'you must not': *Il ne faut pas fumer ici*.
*Il faut* + noun means 'you need': *Il faut deux heures pour aller à Québec* (It takes two hours to get to Quebec City). Add an indirect pronoun for a person: *Il me faut un stylo* (I need a pen).

*Il faut que* + subject + verb also exists; the verb after it is in the subjunctive, which you will learn in lesson 85. For now, notice that with most -er verbs it looks like the present: *Il faut que je travaille*.

learn.tip: Il ne faut pas = you must not (not 'you don't have to'). 'You don't have to' = Tu n'es pas obligé de.

body: *pleuvoir* → *il pleut, il a plu, il pleuvait, il pleuvra, il pleuvrait*. *neiger* → *il neige, il a neigé, il neigeait, il neigera, il neigerait*.
The noun forms: *la pluie* (rain), *la neige* (snow), *la grêle* (hail), *le verglas* (freezing rain, ice), *la tempête* (storm).
Remember the past-tense logic: *Il neigeait quand je suis sorti* (scene, imparfait) vs *Il a neigé toute la nuit* (completed, passé composé).
In Quebec speech, impersonal *il* is usually pronounced *y*: *y pleut*, *y neige*, *y fait froid*. *Il faut* is often reduced to just *faut*: *Faut y aller* (We have to go).

*Il mouille* is the traditional Quebec verb for 'it's raining' (from older French). You will hear *y mouille* constantly. *Y fait frette* means 'it's freezing cold' (informal). *La poudrerie* is blowing snow, and *la slush* (or *la sloche*) is the slushy snow on sidewalks.

quebec.intro: Quebecers talk about the weather constantly. In speech, impersonal 'il' becomes 'y', 'il faut' becomes 'faut', and 'il mouille' (it's raining) is the everyday Quebec verb alongside 'il pleut'.

items.note: Il mouille is traditional Quebec French; y = il in speech
Subjunctive after il faut que comes in lesson 85
Quebec expression: 'raining so hard you could drink standing up'

items.std: Il y a de la neige poussée par le vent.
items.note: Poudrerie is the standard Quebec word

items.std: Il y a de la neige fondante partout.

dialogue.fr: As-tu vu la météo? Y paraît qu'il va neiger cet après-midi.
dialogue.en: Did you see the forecast? Apparently it's going to snow this afternoon.

Oui, et ce soir, il va y avoir du verglas.
dialogue.en: Yes, and tonight there's going to be freezing rain.

dialogue.fr: Bon, il faut que je quitte le bureau plus tôt.
dialogue.en: OK, I have to leave the office earlier.

dialogue.fr: Moi aussi. Et il faudrait pelleter l'entrée avant.
dialogue.en: Me too. And we should shovel the driveway first.

speak.prompt: Describe today's weather and tomorrow's forecast.

speak.prompt: Say three things you must do (il faut) before winter in Quebec.
speak.model: Il faut installer les pneus d'hiver, il faut acheter une pelle et il faut sortir les manteaux.

speak.prompt: Say 'It's raining and it's freezing' casually, the Quebec way.
speak.model: Y mouille pis y fait frette!

write.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences about your worst winter day in Quebec: the weather, what you had to do, and what happened.
write.model: C'était en janvier. Il faisait moins trente et il y avait de la poudrerie. Il a neigé toute la nuit, alors le matin il a fallu pelleter pendant une heure. Ensuite, il y avait du verglas sur les trottoirs et je suis tombé. Il a fallu prendre un taxi pour aller au travail. Si seulement il faisait toujours chaud!
